### 1. Scene
A mixed plate with four small pizza pieces, chopped cooked chicken, pineapple chunks, cherry tomatoes, and dark olives.

### 2. Vessel
A large, rounded rectangular/oval dinner plate, approximately **30 × 24 cm**. Using an equivalent circular diameter of **27 cm** gives:
**Area = 3.14 × 13.5² ≈ 572 cm².**
The separate plate at the left is excluded.

### 3. Items
- Pizza with cheese, tomato sauce, ham, pineapple, and red onion; toppings are included in the pizza estimate.
- Chopped cooked chicken, apparently mostly breast.
- Separate pineapple chunks.
- Cherry tomatoes.
- Dark olives.

No distinct added dressing or oil is clearly visible.

### 4–7. Area, volume, weight, and energy
Volumes represent the outer envelopes of the food piles; bulk density is applied once.

| Item | Plate coverage | Area (cm²) | Height (cm) | Gross volume (ml) | Density (g/ml) | Weight (g) | kcal/100 g | Energy (kcal) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Pizza, including toppings | 39% | 223 | 1.4 | 312 | 0.9 | 281 | 250 | 703 |
| Cooked chicken | 28% | 160 | 1.3 | 208 | 0.9 | 187 | 165 | 309 |
| Pineapple chunks | 11% | 63 | 2.3 | 145 | 0.6 | 87 | 50 | 44 |
| Cherry tomatoes | 7% | 40 | 2.5 | 100 | 0.6 | 60 | 18 | 11 |
| Dark olives | 3% | 17 | 2.0 | 34 | 0.7 | 24 | 145 | 35 |

**Coverage check:** 39 + 28 + 11 + 7 + 3 = **88%**, consistent with a mostly covered plate.

### 8. Sanity check
The estimated **639 g and approximately 1,100 kcal** are plausible for a substantial plate containing four pizza pieces and a sizeable pile of chicken. Pizza thickness and the plate’s actual dimensions are the largest uncertainties.
